title: Ledger record: grade
description: A first-class OPINION record: a bounded rating and a free-text rationale evaluating a completed run/attempt, recorded against the evaluated actor (issue #28 item 1; PRD §10.4 extended). A grade is never a review's confirm/reject verdict on a claim, and it never carries observed or derived authority under any origin — it states a judgment, not a measurement a runner directly observed or a value a deterministic producer derived. The grading producer is the envelope's `origin`/`authority`, exactly like every other record; the actor being graded is a distinct subject named in `data.evaluated_actor_id`, because the two must never be the same actor (no actor grades its own work) -- the ledger append layer refuses that case beside the PRD §10.4 authority checks. The run being graded is the envelope's `run_id`, since every record is already run-scoped; `data.node_run_ref`/`data.attempt_ref` narrow the evaluation to one node run or attempt when the grade is not about the whole run.

data.$comment: Unlike the Phase 0 record types, a grade's core fields are required rather than documentary: a rating with no named evaluated actor, or an actor with no rating and no rationale, is not a grade.

rating.description: The evaluator's opinion score on a fixed 1-5 scale, bounded so grades stay comparable across actors and evaluators.

rationale.description: Free-text justification for the rating. A number alone is not an opinion record; it must carry the reasoning behind it.

evaluated_actor_id.description: The actor being evaluated. Distinct from the envelope's `origin.actor_id`, which is the grading actor -- the ledger append layer refuses a grade where the two are equal.

node_run_ref.description: The node run being evaluated, when the grade is scoped narrower than the whole run. Distinct from the envelope's `node_run_id`, which names what produced this grade record rather than what it evaluates.

attempt_ref.description: The attempt being evaluated, when the grade is scoped to one attempt rather than the whole node run. Distinct from the envelope's `attempt_id` for the same reason as `node_run_ref`.

category.description: An optional flat tag (e.g. review, audit, explore, implement, docs) carried onto the grade so per-actor aggregates can slice quality by task category (issue #28 item 3). Documentary and not a taxonomy: an absent category is a real answer, not an error.
